settings.title: Settings: folders on this computer
settings.claudeUnencrypted: Other computers on that network can connect now, with the token. The connection is not encrypted (plain HTTP): anyone on the network can read the token and what the editor sends. Fine on a home network you trust; anywhere else, keep 127.0.0.1 and reach it through an SSH tunnel. Only computers on this computer's own network are let in, and scripts stay this computer's Claude's only.
settings.claudeRemoteHint: From another computer, use {0} in that command instead of 127.0.0.1. That name needs a network that answers .local names (mDNS); where it does not, use this computer's address on that network instead.
settings.claudeRemoteHintAddresses: From another computer, use {0} in that command instead of 127.0.0.1, where the network answers .local names (mDNS); or this computer's address, which always works but changes when the network gives it another: {1}.
settings.historyHint: How many changes the history keeps to undo; the oldest go first. Empty or 0: no limit, until the history takes 2 GB of memory. Taken from the next change on.
settings.claudeCodeHint: To connect Claude Code, run this once in a terminal (other MCP clients: the address, with the header):
settings.claudeDesktopHint: Claude Desktop: add this to its configuration (Settings > Developer > Edit Config, claude_desktop_config.json), then restart it. The editor must be running:
settings.noExtension: No mod in the folders above offers one.
settings.driverGl: Draw with the graphics driver's OpenGL
settings.drawingHint: Off (the default): the editor draws through Direct3D, like games do. On: through the graphics driver's OpenGL, as earlier versions did; try it if the 3D view or the map draws wrongly or slowly. Taken when the editor starts again.
settings.badPort: The port for Claude must be a number from 1024 to 65535.
settings.badAddress: The address for Claude must be an IP address written in full (IPv4 as four numbers, IPv6 without a %zone): 127.0.0.1 (this computer only), 0.0.0.0 (every network), or one of this computer's.
settings.badHistorySteps: The history's steps must be a whole number from 0 up (empty or 0: no limit).
settings.claudeHint: Lets Claude (Claude Code, Claude Desktop) look at the map open in the editor and change it from a prompt: shape the ground, paint layers, place objects. From this computer only unless Address says otherwise, with the token below. What it changes stays pending, like your own changes, until you save.
settings.extensionsHint: Plugins teach the editor more: new tools, shapes, ground cuts, data on objects. A plugin is its author's own code, run inside the editor with your rights: turn on only plugins you trust. A file that changes (an update) is turned off until you turn it on again.
settings.languageHint: Taken when the editor starts again. Texts not translated yet show in English. To translate the editor, put a copy of its English texts in {0} under the language's code (fr.json, pt-BR.json…) and translate it: see docs/translating.md.

select.hint.click: Click objects (Ctrl adds or takes out, Shift takes out, Ctrl + Shift takes the row from the last one), or drag a box around them (Ctrl adds, Shift takes out). Drag a selected object to move the selection.
select.hint.keys: , . turn (Shift: 15°) · PgUp PgDn lift (Shift: 1 m) · End drops onto what is under · Del deletes · Esc cancels a move · Alt + drag draws a box over objects · Ctrl+A all · Ctrl+H hides · Shift+F frames

select.hint.middle: The middle of the {0} selected objects; Y is the lowest one, Turn the first one's. Turning turns them all around the middle.
select.hint.one: Map position (m) and turn (degrees, clockwise seen from above).
select.msg.moved: Moved {0} object(s){1}. Ctrl+Z puts them back.
select.msg.resized: Resized {0} object(s). Ctrl+Z puts them back.
select.msg.dropped: Dropped {0} object(s): {1} onto other objects, {2} onto the ground.

select.msg.hidden: Hid {0} object(s) in the view (Alt + H shows them again; nothing changes in the map).
select.msg.buildingFirst: Select a building first (or double-click one).
select.msg.building: Selected the whole building: {0} connected part(s).
select.msg.zoneRemoved: Took {0} object(s) out of the selection ({1} left).
paste.hint.click: Click to place; the copied ground keeps its shape relative to the point you click. Height (or Ctrl + wheel; Shift: 0.1 m) moves the paste up or down: lower a building into a hill, and Clear the site digs it out.
paste.info.none: Nothing copied yet: copy in the Area tool (Ctrl+C) or the Select tool (Ctrl+C).
paste.msg.copiedObjects: Copied {0} object(s). Ctrl+V to paste (R turns, F mirrors).
paste.msg.cutObjects: Cut {0} object(s): gone from here (Ctrl+Z brings them back). Ctrl+V to paste them, here or in another area (R turns, F mirrors).

brush.help.raise: Lift the ground under the brush.
brush.help.lower: Dig the ground down under the brush.
brush.help.flatten: Level the ground to one height.
brush.help.smooth: Even out bumps and sharp edges.
brush.help.natural: Turn flat, tool-made ground into natural-looking bumps.
brush.help.erode: Weather the ground: steep slopes slide down to rest (Thermal), or rain cuts gullies and fills hollows (Water).
brush.help.restore: Bring the ground back to how it was when the map was opened.
brush.help.layer: Paint this layer over the ground.
brush.help.layer1: Remove paint: back to the first layer.
measure.hint.first: Click a first point on the ground.
measure.hint.again: Click again to start a new measurement.
measure.hint.fix: Click to fix the second point.
mask.hint.matches: Only change ground that matches everything below.
mask.hint.limits: No biome selected = all biomes. Leave a box empty for no limit. Alt + Shift + click the ground fills the height range around it (±2 m).
mask.error.flatOnly: Slope max {0}° only lets perfectly flat ground through: empty the box for no limit.
mask.error.slopeRange: Slope min is above max: nothing matches.
mask.error.heightRange: Height min is above max: nothing matches.
mask.error.terrainRange: The map's min is above its max: nothing matches.

brush.msg.erodeWholeMap: The whole map eroded ({0} points changed; Strength sets how much). Ctrl+Z takes it back.
brush.help.hole: Takes the ground away: the mouth of a cave, a pit, a hole a mesh fills. Unreal hides the landscape there (its material needs a Landscape Visibility Mask).
tip.brush.holeFill: The brush puts the ground back where there was a hole.
brush.help.terrace: Pulls the ground into flat shelves a step apart, joined by steep rises: fields on a hillside, rice-paddy steps, a stepped quarry.
brush.msg.wholeMap: {0} painted over the whole map ({1} points). Turn the Mask on to paint only some ground.
brush.msg.wholeMapMask: {0} painted where the Mask lets it ({1} points).
brush.msg.notLoaded: Choose a loaded picture as Shape first (built-in stamps stay).
brush.label.targetFromClick: Level to the height where the stroke starts
brush.msg.newPattern: New natural pattern. The next Naturalize stroke or natural path uses it.
brush.msg.stampLoaded: Loaded the stamp “{0}”: white parts work fully, black parts not at all.
brush.msg.stampedUp: Stamped {0} m up. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
brush.msg.stampedDown: Stamped {0} m down. Ctrl+Z undoes it.
brush.pickStamp: Use a grayscale picture as the brush shape
brush.msg.unreadable: That picture could not be read.

view.msg.pickKind: Click an object to pick its kind for {0}. Esc cancels.

history.none: No changes yet in this session.

save.ask.save.title: Save the map
start.tagline: A world editor for Unreal Engine.
start.page.mapsText: Each map is a folder: its ground, colours, rivers and objects. Open one to edit it; with Live on, Unreal follows every change.
start.card.missing: Not found: its folder is gone or was moved
start.empty.title: Start here
start.empty.steps:
1. New map… makes a map from a style's sliders, or over a heightmap from another terrain tool.
2. Open map folder… adds a map made elsewhere. A map folder or a heightmap dropped on this page does the same.
3. With the Groundwork Bridge plugin in your Unreal project, Live sends every change to the level as you make it.
claude.msg.tookAway: Claude took {0} object(s) away; Ctrl+Z puts them back.
claude.msg.stamp: Claude pressed a stamp into {0} ground point(s); Ctrl+Z takes it back.
claude.msg.copies.one: Claude made {0} copy; Ctrl+Z takes it back.
claude.msg.copies.many: Claude made {0} copies; Ctrl+Z takes them back.
claude.msg.moved: Claude moved {0} object(s); Ctrl+Z puts them back.
claude.msg.placed: Claude placed {0} object(s); Ctrl+Z puts them back.
tip.top.map: Back to the start page. What is not saved stays pending.
tip.top.save: Write the changes into the map's files (Ctrl+S). The history stays: undo a step and save again to take it back.
tip.top.history: Every change of this session: roll back to any point, or remove one change (L).
tip.top.view: Show or hide kinds of objects on the map, and the look options (V).
tip.brush.size: Brush radius in metres, up to 300. [ and ] (or Ctrl+wheel) change it by a tenth.
tip.brush.strength: How fast the brush works while you hold the mouse button.
tip.brush.shape: Shape of the brush: circle, square, ring (only a band around the middle: rims and moats), ragged (a noisy edge for natural-looking strokes), or a picture (stamps).
tip.brush.falloff: How the effect fades from the middle to the edge: smooth, linear, dome (round top), flat top (full strength almost to the edge), peak (strong in the middle only), or sharp edge (full strength right to the edge: steep walls, like the pickaxe).
tip.brush.turn: Turn of a square brush or a picture (degrees).
tip.brush.loadStamp: Load a picture (PNG, JPEG...) as a brush shape: white parts work fully, black parts not at all. It is kept for next time.
tip.brush.forgetStamp: Forget the loaded picture chosen as Shape (built-in stamps stay).
tip.brush.terraceStep: How far apart the shelves are, in height.
tip.brush.wholeMap: The whole map in one step, where the Mask lets it (by height, slope, paint): Paint lays its layer (sand on every beach, rock on every cliff), Erode weathers it all at the Strength set. Without the Mask: everywhere.
tip.brush.stampOnce: With a stamp as Shape, a click of Raise or Lower puts the whole stamp into the ground at once, to the Height below, instead of painting.
tip.brush.stampHeight: How high (Raise) or deep (Lower) the white parts of the stamp go (m).
tip.brush.targetFromClick: On: Flatten levels to the height of the ground where you start the stroke. Off: it levels to the Height below.
tip.brush.target: The height (m) Flatten levels to when the option above is off. Alt + click the ground to pick its height.
tip.natural.amp: How tall the natural bumps are (m).
tip.natural.size: How wide the natural bumps are (m): small values give rough ground, large values gentle swells.
tip.natural.seed: Pick a new random bump pattern for the next Naturalize stroke or natural path.
tip.erode.thermal: Thermal: where the ground is steeper than the rest angle, it slides down to its neighbours (screes, softened cliffs).
tip.erode.water: Water: rain drops run downhill, dig where they speed up and leave what they carry where they slow down (gullies, fans, smooth valleys).
tip.erode.rest: Thermal: the steepest slope that stays put (degrees). Lower values flatten more.
tip.mask.on: Limit brushes, paths, area actions and placing to ground that matches all the settings below.
tip.mask.hmin: Only ground at or above this height (m). Empty = no limit. Alt + Shift + click fills the range around a spot.
tip.mask.hmax: Only ground at or below this height (m). Empty = no limit.
tip.mask.smin: Only ground at least this steep (degrees). Empty = no limit.
tip.mask.smax: Only ground at most this steep (degrees). Empty = no limit; 0 lets only perfectly flat ground through.
tip.mask.paint: Only ground with this paint (the map's layers).
tip.mask.terrain: Only ground where a terrain map (as Export the terrain maps writes them) is in the range below: forests on wet ground, rocks on ridges, snow plants where snow lies.
tip.mask.tmin: The map's lowest value that passes, 0 to 1. Empty = no limit.
tip.mask.tmax: The map's highest value that passes, 0 to 1. Empty = no limit.
tip.select.delete: Remove the selected objects from the map (Del). Ctrl+Z brings them back.
tip.select.building: Add every building part connected to the selected ones, through parts that touch (double-clicking one does it too).
tip.select.same: Select every shown object in the area of the kinds that are selected now (all the beeches, all the chests...).
tip.select.all: Select every shown object in the area (Ctrl + A). Alt + A clears the selection.
tip.select.hide: Hide the selected objects in the view (Ctrl + H), to reach what they cover: they are not drawn or picked, and nothing changes in the map.
tip.select.unhide: Show the objects hidden in the view again (Alt + H).
tip.select.invert: Select every shown object in the area that is not selected now, and only those.
tip.select.ground: On: trees, rocks and other objects each land on what is under them where they end up (a floor, a table, a rock no taller than themselves), else on the ground; buildings move as one block that keeps its shape, with its bottom layer on what is under it. Off: the whole selection moves as one block that keeps its shape, as high above the ground under its middle as it was.
tip.select.picks: What clicks, boxes and zones pick, as Unity's pick toggles: everything shown; only buildings (a box over a house leaves its trees and rocks); or only nature (trees, rocks, bushes, plants). What is left out is still drawn, but not picked and not in the way of what is behind it.
tip.select.through: On: a box on the screen also takes what is hidden behind others inside it (inside a house, behind a wall), like Blender's X-ray. Off: only what is seen. Alt + Z switches it.
tip.select.zone: What a drag on empty ground, or Alt + drag over objects, draws. A box on the screen picks only the objects seen inside it, not those behind others: look at a building from the side or from above to pick one floor, one wall or its roof. A zone on the ground picks everything above it, from the ground up.
tip.select.x: Map position east-west (m) of the selection's middle (or of the one object).
tip.select.y: Height (m) of the lowest selected object.
tip.select.turn: Turn (degrees, clockwise seen from above) of the first selected object; the others turn with it around the middle.
tip.select.size: Size of the first selected object; Move there gives them all this size, Move by multiplies each one's own by it.
tip.select.apply: Move and turn the selection to the typed values (one undo step). No snapping on top of typed values.
tip.select.by: Type amounts to move and turn by, instead of where to go.
tip.select.to: The kind to put in place of each selected object.
tip.select.replace: Replace every selected object by the chosen kind, at the same place and facing.
tip.select.pick: Pick the kind from the map: click an object to put its kind in the list (Esc cancels).
tip.select.saved: Selections kept for this map. They are found again by kind and position, also after the map is saved.
tip.select.keep: Keep the selection under a name, to pick it again later.
tip.select.load: Select the objects of this saved selection (instead of the current selection).
tip.select.add: Add the objects of this saved selection to the current selection.
tip.paste.ground: Paste the ground the buildings stood on (under each part and a metre around), blended into the ground here.
tip.paste.offset: Move the pasted ground and objects up or down (m); Ctrl + wheel too (Shift: 0.1 m). Lower a building into a hill: Clear the site digs the ground in its way.
tip.paste.turn: Turn the paste a quarter turn (R). , and . or Alt + wheel turn it by 1° (Shift: 15°).
tip.paste.copies: How many copies one click places, side by side (like WorldEdit's //stack). 1 = a single paste.
tip.paste.along: Which way the copies follow each other: along the copy's width or depth (turning with it), or stacked upwards.
tip.paste.gap: Space left between two copies (m); negative values make them overlap.
tip.place.search: Filter the list of kinds by name.
tip.view.steep: Draw the ground steeper than this many degrees red: where a player cannot walk up (35° to 45° in most games), where cliffs are.
tip.view.seeThrough: Make buildings half see-through, to see the ground and objects inside them.
tip.view.res3d: How many pixels the 3D view draws. Sharp: the screen's own. Balanced: one per screen point. Fast: fewer still. Fewer pixels give more frames per second.
tip.view.unsaved: A green dot over each new object not saved (or applied) yet. Off: no dots (the objects stay).
tip.view.defaults: Back to the default switches (spoilers off).
tip.view.ground: Show only the ground: every kind of object, the water and the overlays off.
tip.view.perf: Write the frame rate to a log file, a line every 0.2 s while the view is used. Off each time the editor opens.
tip.map.save: Write every pending change into the map's files.
tip.start.releases: What each version brought, on GitHub.
tip.start.search: Narrows the cards to the names holding this; Enter opens the first one shown.
tip.start.missing: This map's folder is not there any more: put it back, or take the map off the list (right-click).
tip.start.sample: Opens the Meadow map that comes with the editor's sources.
tip.start.settings: The editor's settings: language, history, Claude's connection.
tip.start.openMap: Opens this map: its ground, colours, rivers and objects.
tip.start.newMap: Makes a new map in the maps folder: asks its name, its size and whether its ground is rolling or flat.
tip.start.openMapFolder: Opens a map folder (one with map.json) and adds it to your maps.
tip.start.docs: The editor's documentation, in its own window (F1 on any page opens it at what you are using): how to start, every tool, and answers to common questions.
tip.start.log: Opens the editor's log (Groundwork.log, started over at each run). Attach it to a bug report on GitHub: it says what the editor did and what went wrong.
tip.history.claude: Takes out every change Claude made in this area's history and keeps yours, even those made after them. Claude's changes made in other areas stay: open those areas to take them back there.
tip.history.older: Shows the next older changes of the history.
tip.history.byClaude: Claude made this change (Settings: Allow Claude to connect).
tip.settings.driverGl: Windows: on, the 3D view and the map draw with the graphics driver's own OpenGL; off (the default), with Direct3D. Taken when the editor starts again.
tip.settings.language: The language the editor shows: the computer's own when there is a translation of it, else English. Taken when the editor starts again.
tip.settings.extension: On: this mod's editor extension runs in the editor (its own code). Off: it does not.
tip.settings.claude: On: the editor takes Claude's requests (MCP) on this computer, from callers with the token below. Off: none.
tip.settings.claudePort: The port Claude connects to, at the Address.
tip.settings.claudeAddress: Where Claude can connect from: pick one, or type an address. 127.0.0.1 (the default): this computer only. 0.0.0.0: every network this computer is on. One of its networks' addresses: that network only. A Claude on another computer then connects to this computer's name or address instead of 127.0.0.1 (the hint under the command says which). The token is asked for either way, but it travels unencrypted: choose another address only on a network you trust, or use an SSH tunnel to 127.0.0.1 instead.
tip.settings.historySteps: How many steps of the history are kept to undo (empty or 0: no limit).
tip.settings.claudeCommand: The command that adds the editor to Claude Code (claude mcp add). It holds the token: keep it to yourself.
tip.settings.claudeDesktop: Claude Desktop starts this program with --mcp-stdio: it passes Claude's messages to the running editor (no second window).
tip.settings.claudeToken: Another token: Claude must be added again with the new command (the old one stops working once saved).
tip.dialog.text: Type the answer, then press OK (Enter).
tip.docs.back: Back to the page shown before (Alt + Left).
tip.docs.home: The help's first page: where to start, and every page.
tip.docs.browser: This page on GitHub, in your web browser.
tip.docs.search: Looks through every page of the help (Ctrl + F). Enter opens the first result.
tip.docs.topic: Help on this: opens its page in the Help window (F1 opens the help on what you are using).
tip.kind.Trees: Trees, logs and stumps: the catalog's Trees.
tip.kind.Rocks: Rocks and boulders: the catalog's Rocks.
tip.kind.Bushes: Bushes and shrubs: the catalog's Bushes.
tip.kind.Plants: Plants, flowers and grass: the catalog's Plants.
tip.kind.Props: Props: crates, fences and other things people made (the catalog's Props).
tip.kind.Buildings: Buildings and their parts: the catalog's Buildings.
tip.kind.Markers: Markers: spawn points, triggers and other placeholders (the catalog's Markers).
tip.kind.Other: Every object whose asset the map's catalog puts in no kind above.
tip.view.models: Draw objects with their models. Off: boxes, faster.
